### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **54** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), AuthRequestTransport (symbol, a top-level interface), IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface), recordMcpAccessTokenUse (symbol, a method of class AuthManager; a method of interface IAuthService), remoteAddress (symbol, a field of interface AuthRequestTransport), resolveClientAddress (symbol, a method of interface IAuthService), getApi (literal, a string literal in RequestAuthService), isAuthGateActive (literal, a string literal in RequestAuthService), resolveClientAddress (literal, a string literal in RequestAuthService))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx`  _(via ipAddress (symbol, a field of interface CredentialUseClient), userAgent (symbol, a field of interface CredentialUseClient))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via sys_api_key (literal, a string literal in stampAdmittedKey))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via sys_api_key (literal, a string literal in stampAdmittedKey))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via sys_api_key (literal, a string literal in stampAdmittedKey))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via resolveExecutionContext (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via userAgent (symbol, a field of interface CredentialUseClient))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via sys_api_key (literal, a string literal in stampAdmittedKey))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via sys_api_key (literal, a string literal in stampAdmittedKey))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **190** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a15b544d542fa3eda258732999778b69613618bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `74fc1b3d73b5bc6c56f97262b92a4b9ecf12c509` — the merge of head `d98b73c4e0d52bc1d323c36e10d542e5657ee3b3` into base `a15b544d542fa3eda258732999778b69613618bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 74fc1b3d73b5bc6c56f97262b92a4b9ecf12c509 && git checkout 74fc1b3d73b5bc6c56f97262b92a4b9ecf12c509
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a15b544d542fa3eda258732999778b69613618bd d98b73c4e0d52bc1d323c36e10d542e5657ee3b3 && git checkout -B drift-repro a15b544d542fa3eda258732999778b69613618bd && git merge --no-ff d98b73c4e0d52bc1d323c36e10d542e5657ee3b3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a15b544d542fa3eda258732999778b69613618bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a15b544d542fa3eda258732999778b69613618bd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31897 (Fixes #31821) · 2026-11-09T10:44Z

Head-sha: `df1a1a1a`

- **Form:** draft to `main`. The whole card lands here under `Fixes #31821`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: `IAuthService` gains the optional `resolveClientAddress(transport)`, and `recordMcpAccessTokenUse` gains an optional `transport` argument (the new type `AuthRequestTransport`). These are `contracts/` changes under #31424 rule 2. `Metadata-protocol: none`. Patch changeset for seven packages.
- **Rulings followed:** Q1 R and Q2 A (amendment 6735816651). Core asks the auth service, so plugin-auth's `resolveClientAddress` stays the one rule that reads `trustProxy`. REST, the runtime dispatcher (with its `/mcp` face) and stdio hand over their facts. Every other key-admitting door records its user agent and `ip_address_absent: 'not_supplied'`; the 13 doors are listed and filed as #31898. The facts reach plugin-audit's `afterUpdate` writer through a core `AsyncLocalStorage` scope that `stampAdmittedKey` opens around its own update only, following `request-grants-memo.ts`. No admission verdict reads the new inputs.
- **Seat answers to the open questions:**
  1. Store the established text, as recommended.
  2. `transport` stays optional here. Whether it becomes required is decided in #31898, once every door hands facts over.
  3. The names `ip_address_absent` and `stdio` / `undetermined` / `not_supplied` / `unrecordable` are accepted, and so is the type name `AuthRequestTransport`.
  4. A second address inside one window stays invisible. The changeset says so, and the window's first use stands (CONTROL pinned). Changing the window is not this card.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION confirmed by this record.** `.changeset/31796-credential-use-audit.md` is pending in the same release. Its sentence "Not yet on the row: the source address and the user agent (`ip_address` / `user_agent` are null) … they follow in a separate change" would be false once this lands. It now reads "Where the use came from: … recorded by the change that follows this one in the same release; see its entry." `check-empty-changeset`'s exit 1 on that note is this class, and the correction stands.
- **Pins and ablations:** 19 ablation legs, CONTROLs included, are each red on their intended assertion. The out-of-scope stamp pin (`not_supplied`, never a guess) is in.
- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31897`: NOT governed, 915 changed lines. K = 10 first-parent commits on `main` since the PR base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates: 101 derived, 101 run, 100 exit 0, plus `check-empty-changeset` confirmed above. tsc passes on all seven packages, and eslint on the touched directories exits 0. CI on this head is running; auto-merge waits for it.
- **Security:** a pre-existing weakness found during the work was reported privately to the seat and routed off GitHub.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31821, `pm:dispatched` removed, the card closed by `Fixes`, and #31898 moved to `pm:queue`.
